ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Bed rest, warmth and time; tending eases it a little, but nothing cures it. A cold passes in about a week, a chest cold or a lingering cough in one or two. Keep the old and the frail warm and fed, so it doesn't turn into pneumonia.
Rest and plenty to drink. It's over in two or three days, and tending shortens it.
Have a doctor tend it; industrial medicine or better works best on both. Hay fever settles twice as fast indoors while the plants are in flower, so give them indoor work.
Rest and quiet. Most shake it off in five or six days, and medicine does little for it.
A day or two in bed at the start, then light work until it heals; for sore hands, a break from the bench. Tending speeds all three along.
They heal on their own, in a few days to a week. A proper bed prevents a stiff neck; warm clothes, chilblains; a hat, sunburn.

Fix the cause: move a wood fire out of a small room, light the workbench, and keep bedrooms clean, dry and roofed. Clean air clears the coughs in days, a night's sleep clears tired eyes, and tending eases rimrot and ash lung.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Fix their rooms' air and light

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: One treatment from a doctor settles it within a day or two. Fewer sweets make it less likely to come back.
Rest, good food and time. Time in bed gets them well about a third sooner; back at work too soon, they can set themselves back a couple of days.

Keep the patient in bed and tended as often as possible, with the best medicine the colony has. Hover over the illness in their Health tab for what helps it most: for tuberculosis, treatment every day without a gap; for cholera, someone to keep them drinking. The catching ones spread to whoever shares the room, so let them sleep apart.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Keep them in bed and tended

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Fruit or vegetables, raw or cooked into meals. Nothing else cures it, and it clears within a couple of weeks of eating them again.
It passes in two days. Good medicine on the shelf and a second doctor make a hard case lighter to carry.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: It comes from seeing someone through a serious illness.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Add the "remove appendix" operation in their Health tab; any doctor can do it, with two medicine. Until it's done, tend them as often as possible.
Treat the bite every day, without a gap, until the danger has passed: treatment only works before the fever comes. Industrial medicine or better works fastest.

None of these can kill. Tending eases a kidney stone or shingles and speeds it along, industrial medicine most of all; nerve pain needs only warmth and rest. A stone passes within a week, shingles in two or three, nerve pain in one or two.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Tend it to ease the pain

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Rest in a dark, quiet room. A migraine passes twice as fast lying down, and insomnia in a week or so with a regular bedtime and no work after dark. A doctor can help with either. Fewer late nights, regular meals and less to worry about keep them away.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Give them a dark, quiet room

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Hiccups, heartburn and a nosebleed pass within hours, travel sickness within a day of stopping. A splinter can take a week to work its way out, but any doctor picks it out in one go.

They heal on their own, from a day or two for heat rash and frostnip to a week or two for a rash or athlete's foot, and a doctor's salve eases most of them. Long sleeves and a net over the bed in swamps and jungles, gloves in the fields, a cooler bedroom in the heat, dry socks, and a scarf and mittens in bitter cold prevent them.
Have a doctor treat them, which clears them in a day or two, then clean the room they sleep in: lice spread in dirty rooms, and they carry typhus.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Treat them, then clean their room

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: What the flu or the plague left behind. Warm drinks and a warm room at night for the cough, clean dressings and rest for the swellings; a doctor's tending speeds both a little. They pass in a week or two.
A healed break or burn settling. Walking on the leg (not bed rest) and a doctor's strapping shorten a limp; a salve calms an itching burn. Both pass in a week or two.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Strap the limp, salve the burn

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: The fight or the horror, coming back at night. It can't be tended; company in the evening and an ordinary day's work help it pass within a few days to a week. Strong walls and fewer fights at the door mean fewer bad nights.

The place itself. Gas masks on polluted ground (and cleaning it up), goggles or a full helmet on bright snow, high boots in the swamp; in orbit, plain food and regular hours while the body settles. All pass in hours to a few days, and a doctor's tending helps.
